author: OpenAxolotl maintainer (concept and Meshy generation), rigged in-repo by the project's headless Blender pipeline
tool: Meshy (image-to-3D) from a ChatGPT-authored concept image, both run by the maintainer OUTSIDE this repository; the export was then brought inside by three headless Blender 4.0.2 passes that are in the repository and reproducible: tools/decimate_model.py (welds the seam-split shell, collapse-decimates 1,933,518 triangles to 55,000, downscales both 4096 maps to 2048, and gates on two-way surface deviation and on open edges), tools/blender/fit_hero_rig.py (corrects an 18.7-degree yaw in the export, normalises the model into the reference hero's authoring frame, and fits the 12-bone table to this creature's own anatomy), and tools/rig_model.py (bone-heat weights, unweighted vertices adopted by their nearest bone, nine animation clips). The clips were later rebuilt in place through that tool's --clips-only mode, which rekeys the armature and touches neither geometry nor weights: the walk cycle had been keying the legs on the axis that LIFTS a foot rather than the one that swings it, so all four feet rose and fell together and none of them ever stepped, and the swimming legs were frozen at a constant. The triangle count is unchanged at 25,000.
prompt: Generated by the maintainer in Meshy from a ChatGPT concept image; the exact Meshy prompt is theirs and is not recorded in this repository. The source export is kept at reference/hero/pink_axolotl_2.glb so every step above can be re-run from it. Matched against the maintainer's own reference sheet, reference/hero/01_hero_perspective.png. SUPERSEDES the previous shipped hero, which was built procedurally in-repo by tools/blender/make_axolotl.py as vertex-coloured geometry across five role meshes; that generator remains in the repository and still produces a valid character, but it is no longer what ships. The two are not the same creature: normalised by body length the generated hero is 0.487 tall against this one's 0.256, a chunky upright toy against a flat sprawling axolotl, which is why the hand-authored bone table could not be reused and a fitter was written instead.
licenseTerms: Meshy's terms of service govern the generated mesh and its maps; the maintainer generated the asset under their own Meshy account and contributed it to this repository. The in-repo Blender passes that decimate, fit and rig it are Apache-2.0 with the rest of the project, but they do not change the terms on the geometry they transform. REVIEW NEEDED before any redistribution of the project that assumes a uniform Apache-2.0 grant over assets/: this is the first shipped asset whose terms come from an external generator rather than from a script in this repository.
